narratives.name: Platform Context
narratives.description: OpenShift platform infrastructure architecture and evolution

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift platform infrastructure builds on enterprise Kubernetes with Red Hat's hardened operating system (RHCOS), integrated GitOps, and operator-driven automation. Platform engineers architect high availability control planes, security-hardened network isolation, and multi-cluster fleet management to deliver resilient foundation for cloud-native workloads.

Key platform concepts include the immutable RHCOS operating system, CRI-O container runtime, etcd distributed key-value store for cluster state, and the operator pattern for automated lifecycle management. Private clusters isolate API endpoints from public internet while bastion hosts control administrative SSH access.

Architectural decisions include minimum three-node control planes for quorum-based fault tolerance, dedicated infrastructure nodes separating platform services from application workloads, and multi-zone deployment for geographic resilience. GitOps with Argo CD eliminates manual cluster configuration drift, and Machine Operator enables remote management without SSH access. Multi-cluster evolution leverages Advanced Cluster Management for centralized policy enforcement, observability aggregation, and disaster recovery orchestration.

Success depends on treating infrastructure as code through GitOps, replacing manual operations with versioned software, and systematically eliminating toil through automation investment aligned with SRE principles.

Platform engineers provision clusters with Infrastructure as Code, implement GitOps configuration management, and establish automated operational workflows replacing manual scripting with versioned software.
Day-2 operations leverage automated cluster lifecycle management, self-service provisioning, dynamic storage allocation, and zero-downtime updates orchestrated through GitOps pull-based agents.
Multi-cluster fleet management with Advanced Cluster Management, predictive capacity planning, error budget tracking, and systematic toil elimination achieve operational excellence at scale.

narratives.name: Way Of Working Context
narratives.description: SRE-driven operational practices evolution

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift platform operations adopt SRE principles distinguishing between toil (manual, repetitive work) and engineering (building automation). Teams transition from script-based operations to versioned software with CI/CD testing, GitOps configuration management, and self-service workflows eliminating ticket-driven provisioning.

Key SRE concepts include toil budgeting (maximum 50% of engineering time on operational work), error budgets as a contract between reliability and velocity, symptom-based alerting targeting SLOs rather than causes, and the principle that operations code must be tested via CI/CD pipelines like any other software.

Foundation establishment requires replacing manual shell scripts with versioned operations code tested via CI/CD pipelines, adopting GitOps with Argo CD for cluster configuration management, and defining self-service workflows that eliminate manual approvals. Teams implement symptom-based alerting aligned to Service Level Objectives rather than cause-based alerts generating noise, track error budgets transparently with stakeholders, and systematically identify toil for automation investment. Multi-cluster management via Argo CD ApplicationSets standardizes configuration options across fleet, preventing snowflake clusters and configuration drift.

Operational excellence emerges when toil is systematically eliminated through software engineering practices, teams own and operate the automation they build, and chaos engineering validates resilience assumptions.

narratives.name: Storage Infrastructure Context
narratives.description: Persistent storage architecture and maturity progression

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift persistent storage decouples data lifecycle from pod lifecycle, enabling stateful applications like databases, message queues, and file servers. Storage infrastructure maturity progresses from manual pre-provisioning through self-service dynamic allocation to distributed storage systems with cross-cluster capabilities.

Core storage concepts include PersistentVolumes (PV) as cluster-level storage resources, PersistentVolumeClaims (PVC) as application-level storage requests, StorageClasses as dynamic provisioning templates, and Container Storage Interface (CSI) drivers as the standard plugin mechanism for storage backends.

Static provisioning requires administrators to manually create PersistentVolume resources matched to PersistentVolumeClaims, suitable for initial adoption but limiting agility. Dynamic provisioning via StorageClasses enables self-service volume allocation with technology-specific parameters. Advanced storage services like OpenShift Data Foundation provide Ceph-based distributed storage with multi-zone replication, snapshots, clones, and encryption at rest. Hybrid cloud evolution spans on-premises and cloud with object storage integration and cross-cluster migration capabilities.

Success depends on selecting appropriate storage technologies for workload characteristics, implementing monitoring and alerting on capacity and performance, and protecting data through snapshots and disaster recovery procedures.

narratives.name: GitOps Context
narratives.description: GitOps configuration management principles and implementation

narrativeContexts.context: GitOps embodies infrastructure-as-code principles by maintaining desired cluster state in Git repositories with automated synchronization, eliminating manual kubectl/oc apply operations, configuration drift, and providing audit trails through Git history.

Core GitOps concepts include declarative configuration (desired state in YAML manifests), pull-based reconciliation (agents poll for changes rather than accepting pushes), self-healing (automatic reversion of manual changes), and the Application custom resource as the unit of deployment management in Argo CD.

Git-stored configuration establishes Git as single source of truth with directory structures organizing manifests by environment and namespace. Automated sync via Argo CD Application resources monitors Git repositories and applies updates automatically. Self-healing enables automatic reversion of manual cluster changes and RBAC restrictions preventing direct modifications. Fleet management scales to multi-cluster environments using ApplicationSet generators and Argo CD Agent architecture for pull-based GitOps where remote clusters poll control plane.

Operational excellence requires enforcing Git as authoritative source through self-healing and RBAC, documenting emergency break-glass procedures for critical incidents, and implementing progressive rollout strategies testing changes in non-production before production deployment.

narratives.name: Cluster Lifecycle Context
narratives.description: Cluster update and upgrade lifecycle management

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift cluster lifecycle management delivers weekly z-stream security patches and periodic y-stream feature upgrades through cluster version operator with signature verification via Sigstore integration, ensuring platform currency while maintaining availability.

Key lifecycle concepts include semantic versioning (major.minor.patch), z-stream updates (security/bug fixes with minimal risk), y-stream updates (feature changes requiring compatibility testing), the cluster version operator (automated update controller), and Sigstore (cryptographic signature verification for update payloads).

Manual updates require etcd backups and post-update validation. Automated scheduling defines maintenance windows while applying z-stream patches automatically and testing canary updates before production. Continuous delivery enables rolling updates with Sigstore verification and automatic rollback. Fleet-wide orchestration coordinates updates across environments with compliance tracking and staged rollout using Advanced Cluster Management.

Zero-downtime updates depend on application workload design (health probes, graceful termination, Pod Disruption Budgets), understanding semantic versioning constraints, and testing canary updates in non-production environments before production rollout.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations need to deploy OpenShift clusters on cloud or on-premises infrastructure, requiring architectural decisions on high availability, network isolation, and security hardening that will determine platform resilience and operational characteristics.
Install and configure OpenShift Container Platform with appropriate cluster topology including IPI vs UPI deployment, private cluster configuration, etcd encryption, and multi-zone distribution.

Generate install-config.yaml via openshift-install create install-config, customize for private clusters with internal load balancers restricting API and ingress to VPN or bastion hosts, enable etcd encryption at rest, and select FIPS-validated cryptography if compliance requires. Run openshift-install create cluster provisioning infrastructure and bootstrapping control plane (approximately 30-45 minutes), then validate installation by checking oc get nodes, oc get co (cluster operators), and accessing web console. Configure post-installation OAuth identity providers, install operators for monitoring/logging/service mesh, establish GitOps for configuration management, and document cluster configuration.

Fully operational OpenShift cluster with high availability control plane, security-hardened network isolation, encrypted etcd, and documented configuration ready for workload onboarding. Platform progresses from Architecture Selected through Provisioned.

activities.name: Implement GitOps Configuration Management
activities.description: Deploy Argo CD for declarative cluster and application configuration from Git repositories.

narratives.name: Implement GitOps Approach
narratives.description: How to implement GitOps configuration management with Argo CD

narrativeContexts.context: Platform teams manage cluster configuration manually via kubectl/oc apply, leading to configuration drift, undocumented changes, and inconsistent state across environments. No automated reconciliation detects or reverts unauthorized manual modifications.
Deploy GitOps configuration management using Argo CD to establish Git as single source of truth with automated synchronization, self-healing, and fleet-wide configuration management.

Install OpenShift GitOps operator via OperatorHub deploying Argo CD instances. Configure Git repository access with SSH keys or HTTPS tokens. Create Application custom resources defining repository URL, target revision, path, and destination. Define sync policies with automatic sync, enable self-healing to revert manual changes, and configure pruning. For fleet management, use ApplicationSets with generators (Git, cluster, list) creating Applications from templates. Implement Argo CD Agent architecture for pull-based GitOps in security-conscious environments, and integrate Image Updater for automated deployment manifest updates.

Declarative configuration management with automated Git-to-cluster synchronization, self-healing drift remediation, fleet-wide ApplicationSet orchestration, and comprehensive audit trail through Git history. GitOps Configuration Management progresses through Automated Sync and Self-Healing states.

activities.name: Perform Cluster Upgrades
activities.description: Update OpenShift cluster to new versions with zero downtime and rollback capability.

narratives.name: Perform Cluster Upgrades Approach
narratives.description: How to perform cluster upgrades with zero downtime

narrativeContexts.context: OpenShift clusters require regular updates including weekly z-stream security patches and periodic y-stream feature upgrades. Manual update processes are error-prone, risk downtime, and cannot scale to multi-cluster fleet management.
Establish automated update scheduling with canary testing, zero-downtime rolling updates with Sigstore signature verification, and fleet-wide orchestration via Advanced Cluster Management.

Check update availability via web console or oc adm upgrade. Back up etcd before updates. Apply z-stream patches automatically via maintenance windows while requiring approval for y-stream upgrades. Test canary updates on non-production clusters first. Enable Sigstore signature verification for core payload validation. Monitor rolling updates with oc get clusterversion and oc get co. Configure Pod Disruption Budgets for application availability during node updates. Use Advanced Cluster Management for staged fleet rollout across development, staging, production environments with compliance tracking.

Zero-downtime cluster updates with cryptographic signature verification, automated rollback on failure, and fleet-wide version compliance tracking. Cluster Lifecycle Management progresses through Automated Update Scheduling and Continuous Delivery.

activities.name: Implement Persistent Storage
activities.description: Configure dynamic storage provisioning with appropriate storage classes for workload requirements.

narratives.name: Implement Persistent Storage Approach
narratives.description: How to implement persistent storage with dynamic provisioning

narrativeContexts.context: Application teams require persistent storage for stateful workloads (databases, message queues, registries) but administrators manually pre-provision PersistentVolumes, creating bottlenecks and limiting self-service capability. No dynamic provisioning or storage tiering exists.
Implement dynamic storage provisioning with CSI drivers, StorageClasses for performance tiers, and OpenShift Data Foundation for advanced distributed storage services.

Install CSI drivers via OperatorHub (AWS EBS, OpenShift Data Foundation). Create StorageClass resources defining provisioners, parameters (volume type, IOPS, throughput), and reclaim policies (Retain for production, Delete for ephemeral). Mark default StorageClass. Enable volume expansion. Implement storage monitoring via Prometheus metrics with alerts on capacity and provisioning failures. Configure VolumeSnapshot resources for data protection. Deploy OpenShift Data Foundation for Ceph-based distributed storage with multi-zone replication, snapshots, and encryption at rest.

Self-service dynamic storage provisioning with performance-tiered StorageClasses, data protection through snapshots and backup integration, and distributed storage services supporting stateful production workloads. Storage Infrastructure progresses through Dynamic Provisioning and Advanced Storage Services.

activities.name: Configure Capacity Management
activities.description: Implement ClusterAutoscaler and resource optimization for right-sized infrastructure.

narratives.name: Configure Capacity Management Approach
narratives.description: How to implement capacity management and optimization

narrativeContexts.context: Clusters are either overprovisioned (wasting resources and budget) or underprovisioned (causing pod scheduling failures and degraded performance). No automated scaling responds to workload demand changes, and no cost optimization practices track infrastructure spending efficiency.
Implement ClusterAutoscaler for dynamic node scaling, ClusterResourceOverride for resource optimization, and FinOps monitoring for cost-aware capacity management.

Configure ClusterAutoscaler with minimum and maximum node counts, with nodes added when pod scheduling fails and removed when underutilized. Limit scaling to 25-50 nodes at once. Configure machine health checks for automatic unhealthy node replacement. Install ClusterResourceOverride operator for overcommitment ratios. Establish ResourceQuota and LimitRanges for multi-tenant cost control. Implement monitoring alerts on resource pressure and rightsizing recommendations based on actual usage. Track sustainability metrics and optimize reserved instance utilization.

Dynamic capacity management with automated node scaling, resource optimization reducing overprovisioning waste, multi-tenant cost controls, and FinOps practices demonstrating infrastructure spending efficiency. Platform progresses toward Evolving state with optimized economics.

narrativeContexts.context: After initial cluster provisioning, the platform needs comprehensive network topology documentation, infrastructure node designation, and security controls establishing the operational baseline before workloads can be accepted.
Define and document the platform baseline including network topology, node types, security perimeters, and integration points.

Document control plane and worker node network topology. Designate infrastructure nodes for platform services separation from application workloads. Define bastion host architecture for SSH access control. Specify dedicated VPC per cluster with restricted firewall rules. Complete master authorized networks design restricting API endpoint access.
Fully documented platform baseline with security-hardened network architecture, designated infrastructure nodes, and controlled access points ready for operational configuration.

activities.name: Decommission Cluster Resources
activities.description: Gracefully decommission clusters with workload migration, data preservation, and resource cleanup.

narratives.name: Decommission Cluster Resources Approach
narratives.description: How to gracefully decommission clusters

narrativeContexts.context: Clusters reach end of life due to hardware refresh, architecture migration, or consolidation. Workloads and data must be preserved during decommissioning to prevent service disruption or data loss.
Execute controlled cluster decommissioning with workload migration, data backup, and infrastructure resource cleanup.

Identify all workloads and persistent data on the target cluster. Execute migration using Migration Toolkit for containers or manual redeployment to destination clusters. Create final application-consistent backups via OADP. Verify workload availability on destination. Remove cluster from GitOps management and ACM fleet. Execute infrastructure teardown via Terraform destroy or cloud provider cleanup. Document decommissioning for compliance audit trail.
Clean decommissioning with zero data loss, all workloads migrated and verified on destination clusters, infrastructure resources reclaimed, and compliance audit trail maintained.

activities.name: Establish SRE Operational Principles
activities.description: Define and adopt SRE principles including toil budgeting, error budgets, and infrastructure-as-code mandates.

narratives.name: Establish SRE Operational Principles Approach
narratives.description: How to establish foundational SRE principles

narrativeContexts.context: Operations teams rely on manual shell scripts, ad-hoc configuration changes, and ticket-based provisioning with no formal principles governing how operational work is approached or measured.
Establish foundational SRE principles defining toil budgets, GitOps standards, infrastructure-as-code mandates, and self-service goals.

Adopt SRE principles limiting toil to 50% of engineering time. Establish GitOps as the configuration management standard. Mandate versioned, tested automation for all infrastructure changes. Define self-service principles eliminating manual ticket-based provisioning. Document principles in team charter and operational playbooks.
Team-agreed operational principles establishing SRE culture with measurable toil budgets, GitOps standards, and infrastructure-as-code mandates guiding all subsequent operational decisions.

narratives.name: Define Operations Automation Framework Approach
narratives.description: How to define the operations automation framework

narrativeContexts.context: SRE principles are established but no concrete automation framework, CI/CD pipeline for operations code, or monitoring strategy connects principles to practice.
Select and configure the automation toolchain including GitOps workflow (Argo CD), CI/CD pipeline for operations code testing, cluster lifecycle automation framework, and monitoring strategy.

Select GitOps workflow with Argo CD for configuration management. Establish CI/CD pipeline for operations code with automated testing. Define cluster lifecycle automation framework covering provisioning, updating, and decommissioning. Align monitoring and alerting strategy to SRE symptom-based approach with Service Level Objectives.
Concrete automation framework established with GitOps workflow, CI/CD pipelines for operations code, lifecycle automation definition, and SLO-aligned monitoring strategy ready for team adoption.

activities.name: Implement Operations-as-Software Practices
activities.description: Transition from ad-hoc scripts to versioned, tested operations software with CI/CD validation.

narratives.name: Implement Operations-as-Software Approach
narratives.description: How to transition operations to versioned software

narrativeContexts.context: Operations automation framework is defined but team still uses legacy scripts and manual procedures. Operations code is not treated as production software with testing, versioning, and release practices.
Migrate operations from ad-hoc scripts to versioned software with CI/CD testing, unit tests, and dedicated infrastructure execution.

Implement operations as versioned software in Git with release strategy. Build CI/CD pipeline that automates testing of operation workflows before deployment. Write unit tests ensuring behavior consistency across changes. Deploy operations on dedicated infrastructure rather than developer machines. Establish code review practices for operational changes matching development rigor.

Operations code treated as production software with automated CI/CD testing, unit test coverage, version control, and dedicated execution infrastructure. Way Of Working transitions from defined to actively used.

activities.name: Track Toil and Optimize SRE Practices
activities.description: Measure operational toil, implement error budget tracking, and systematically improve SRE practices.

narratives.name: Track Toil and Optimize SRE Practices Approach
narratives.description: How to measure and optimize SRE operational practices

narrativeContexts.context: Operations practices are in place but no systematic measurement of toil, error budgets, or operational efficiency validates that SRE principles are achieving intended outcomes. Alert fatigue persists and teams lack visibility into automation ROI.
Implement toil tracking, error budget management, symptom-based alerting optimization, and chaos engineering validation of automation resilience.

Implement toil tracking with classification of operational tasks as toil vs engineering. Track error budgets and communicate consumption transparently to stakeholders. Transition from cause-based to symptom-based alerting aligned with SLOs. Eliminate alert fatigue through severity-based routing and alert quality reviews. Implement chaos engineering experiments validating automation resilience. Establish metrics dashboards demonstrating continuous operational improvement.

Demonstrably effective SRE practices with toil consistently below 50%, transparent error budget tracking, eliminated alert fatigue, and chaos-validated automation resilience. Way Of Working achieves Working Well state.

activities.name: Provision Initial Storage Infrastructure
activities.description: Configure initial persistent storage with manual PersistentVolume provisioning and basic reclaim policies.

narratives.name: Provision Initial Storage Approach
narratives.description: How to configure initial persistent storage infrastructure

narrativeContexts.context: Newly provisioned cluster has no persistent storage configured. Stateful workloads cannot be deployed until PersistentVolumes are manually provisioned and basic storage protections are enabled.
Configure initial persistent storage infrastructure with manual PersistentVolume provisioning, basic storage technologies (NFS, iSCSI, cloud block), and data protection policies.

Create PersistentVolume resources manually matching anticipated workload requirements. Bind PersistentVolumeClaims to pre-provisioned volumes. Configure appropriate storage technologies (NFS for shared access, iSCSI for block, cloud provider volumes for managed infrastructure). Set reclaim policies to prevent accidental data deletion. Enable Storage Object in Use Protection to prevent deletion of PVCs actively bound to pods.
Basic persistent storage operational with manually provisioned volumes, appropriate reclaim policies, and storage protection enabled for initial stateful workload support.

narratives.description: How to create and organize GitOps repository structure

narrativeContexts.context: Cluster configurations exist as ad-hoc files on administrator workstations or in unstructured repositories. No standardized Git structure, PR workflow, or branch strategy governs configuration management.
Create structured Git repository organizing all Kubernetes manifests by environment and namespace with pull request workflows and branch strategies.

Create Git repository with directory structure organizing configurations by environment (dev, staging, production) and namespace. Store all Kubernetes manifests in Git. Establish pull request workflow requiring peer reviews for configuration changes. Define branch strategy controlling promotion between environments. Document Git as single source of truth for cluster state. Configure access controls and branch protection rules.
Structured Git repository established as single source of truth for cluster state with organized directory structure, PR-based change workflows, and branch strategy ready for Argo CD integration.
